attribution: Die Regesten, Kommentare und Registereinträge zu Friedrich I. Barbarossa stammen aus den Regesta Imperii, Abteilung IV,2 (RI IV,2,1–4 und Register), herausgegeben von der Deutschen Kommission für die Bearbeitung der Regesta Imperii bei der Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur Mainz, online in Regesta Imperii Online und als Daten im RI Lab. Sie stehen unter der Lizenz Creative Commons Namensnennung 4.0 International. Verwendet wurden die Registerdatei RI_004-002-RegisterBarbarossa.csv und ein CSV-Export der Regesten, dessen Exportstand noch festzustellen ist. Die Edition hat die Daten verändert. Markup wurde in Klartext überführt, Regesten wurden ausgewählt und verknüpft, und aus dem Regesttext wurden mit einem Large Language Model (LLM) RDF-Aussagen erzeugt. Diese Aussagen, ihre Prüfstände und die Visualisierungen sind Ergebnisse dieses Projekts und keine Aussagen der Regesta Imperii. Die Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur Mainz ist an der Edition nicht beteiligt und hat sie nicht geprüft. Jedes Regest verlinkt auf seine Einzelansicht in Regesta Imperii Online.

gaps.text: No act type for a refusal or rejection of a request: the regest's main act, Friedrich and Konrad III. 'lehnt ... ab' the restitution, is captured only indirectly through the rv:Request factoid with them as addressees; neither restitution nor possession by any party is asserted.
Mediator reference uses the anaphoric wording 'seines König' as name in source; its identification with Ludwig VII. rests on the preceding phrase.
Odo's offices ('Kapellan König Ludwigs VII. von Frankreich und Mönch von St. Denis') are not extracted as rv:OfficeHolding because they are not needed for the claim.
No act type for a refusal or rejection of a request (lehnt ... ab).
Direction of the kinship term 'Oheim' is not expressible with two symmetric rv:Kin references.

findings.subject: urn:regesta:22663:request-restitution
findings.description: The main statement of the regest is the joint refusal by Friedrich and Konrad III. The candidate records only the request and puts the refusal passage into the request's evidence, so the graph does not say that the request was rejected. The contract has no refusal type; at most the claim before rulers could be read as rv:Dispute. The defect is mostly a model gap, but as it stands a query for this factoid returns an open request whose outcome the regest states.
findings.proposal: Under the current contract, record the refusal in the report as a model gap and keep only the second selector as evidence of the request; with a Refusal act type, add an ActFactoid with Friedrich and Konrad as deciding actors, rf:refersToAct to the request and rf:concerns the possessions.

findings.subject: urn:regesta:22663:request-restitution
findings.description: Ludwig VII. as rv:Mediator and Friedrich and Konrad as rv:Addressee are inferences. The regest says Odo wanted to achieve restitution through his king's mediation; it does not name the addressee of the request. The reading is plausible and the file marks it as the producer's reading.
findings.proposal: Keep, with the addressee inference flagged for expert review.

decisions.finding: The joint refusal of restitution by Friedrich and Konrad III., the main statement, is not represented; reviewer suggests trimming the request's evidence to the second selector.
decisions.reason: 'Friedrich lehnt gemeinsam mit seinem Oheim, König Konrad III., die Restitution ... ab' is a refusal, for which the act scheme has no type; rv:Judgment or rv:Revocation would change the meaning. The first selector stays, because the rv:Addressee references for Friedrich and Konrad rest on that passage, as the guideline on a second selector for a role resting on a different passage allows. The file's comment already reports the refusal as a model gap, and no restitution or possession is asserted.

decisions.finding: Ludwig VII. as rv:Mediator and Friedrich and Konrad as rv:Addressee are inferences.
decisions.reason: 'die ... Odo von Deuil, durch die Vermittlung seines König erreichen wollte' supports Mediator for Ludwig VII.; the addressee reading follows from the same sentence, in which Friedrich and Konrad decline the restitution Odo sought. Ludwig stays regest-local because the packet has no candidate for him. The comment marks the addressee reading as the producer's.
